key_insight: The paper finds that frontier AI agents can draft plausible-looking follow-up research papers, but none met all domain-scientist criteria for open scientific problems.
engineering_relevance: For AI materials science workflows, the result shows current agents are not yet reliable for autonomous hypothesis-to-paper research without strong human oversight and validation.
method: Built the "Into the Unknown" benchmark using real unpublished follow-up directions from DOE national lab scientists.
Asked nine frontier agents to generate 15 follow-up papers each across five scientific domains.
Evaluated each submission against scientist-defined conditions and an integrity check for fabricated or contradictory claims.
evidence_signal: Across 135 agent-generated submissions, none satisfied all required conditions and 114 failed integrity checks, often due to unsupported claims or numbers contradicting evidence.
watch_item: The benchmark is promising, but results depend on the specific scientist-defined rubric and may not capture every form of research quality or novelty.
paper_title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
